text: Financial institutions must file a Currency Transaction Report (CTR) for any cash transaction exceeding $10,000 in a single business day, whether a single transaction or multiple transactions that aggregate to more than $10,000.

Under 31 CFR 1010.410, financial institutions must obtain and retain the name, address, and account number of both the originator and beneficiary for wire transfers of $3,000 or more. For wire transfers over $10,000, enhanced recordkeeping and potential SAR filing obligations apply.

A Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) must be filed within 30 days of detecting a suspicious transaction involving $5,000 or more that the institution knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect involves funds from illegal activity, is designed to evade BSA reporting, lacks a lawful purpose, or facilitates criminal activity.

Broker-dealers must establish an AML compliance program including: written policies and procedures, designation of a compliance officer, employee training, and independent testing. The program must be approved by senior management.

A Customer Identification Program (CIP) must, at minimum, collect name, date of birth (for individuals), address, and identification number (SSN for U.S. persons; passport or similar for foreign persons), verify the information, and check OFAC and other government lists.
Large accelerated filers (public float >= $700M) must file Form 10-K within 60 days of fiscal year end. Accelerated filers ($75M-$700M) have 75 days. Non-accelerated filers have 90 days.

Regulation FD (Fair Disclosure) prohibits public companies from selectively disclosing material nonpublic information without simultaneous public disclosure. If selective disclosure occurs, the company must disclose promptly (same day if intentional; within 24 hours if unintentional).

Section 16(b) requires corporate insiders (directors, officers, and 10%+ shareholders) to disgorge profits from purchases and sales of company securities within a 6-month period. Short-swing profits may be recovered by the company or a shareholder derivatively.

Schedule 13D must be filed within 10 days of acquiring beneficial ownership of more than 5% of a class of registered equity securities, disclosing the filer's identity, source of funds, purpose, interest in securities, and related contracts.

SEC Rule 10b-5 prohibits using material nonpublic information to trade securities or tipping others who trade. Information is material if a reasonable investor would consider it important, and nonpublic until disseminated to investors generally.

Regulation T requires customers to deposit initial margin of 50% for equity purchases. FINRA Rule 4210 sets maintenance margin at 25% of long market value. Pattern day traders must maintain minimum equity of $25,000.

FINRA Rule 4512 requires member firms to maintain essential customer account facts: name and residence, whether of legal age, the registered representative's name, and for non-institutional accounts the customer's occupation and tax ID/SSN.

FINRA Rule 2111 requires a reasonable basis to believe a recommended transaction or strategy is suitable based on the customer's investment profile, including age, financial situation, tax status, objectives, experience, time horizon, liquidity needs, and risk tolerance.

SEC Rule 17a-4 requires broker-dealers to preserve certain records for at least 6 years (3 years in an easily accessible place for some records). Electronic records must use WORM (Write Once, Read Many) storage.

FINRA Rule 3110 requires each member to maintain a supervisory system reasonably designed to achieve compliance, including written supervisory procedures (WSPs), a designated supervisory principal, and review of correspondence and customer accounts.

FINRA Rule 5310 requires broker-dealers to use reasonable diligence to obtain best execution, considering price, speed of execution, likelihood of execution, order size, and the nature of the transaction.

Under Basel III as implemented by the OCC, national banks must maintain a CET1 ratio of at least 4.5%, Tier 1 ratio of at least 6%, total capital ratio of at least 8%, and leverage ratio of at least 4%. Well-capitalized thresholds are higher (CET1 6.5%, Tier 1 8%, total 10%, leverage 5%).

OCC Bulletin 2013-29 requires third-party risk management commensurate with risk and complexity: due diligence before entering relationships, contract provisions for performance and audit rights, ongoing monitoring, and contingency planning, with enhanced due diligence for critical activities.

National banks with total consolidated assets between $10 billion and $100 billion must conduct annual stress tests under baseline, adverse, and severely adverse scenarios and report results to the OCC.

The Volcker Rule prohibits banking entities from proprietary trading for their own account to profit from short-term price movements. Permitted exceptions include market making, underwriting, hedging, trading in government obligations, and insurance activities.

Banking entities are prohibited from acquiring ownership interests in or sponsoring covered funds (hedge funds, private equity), with limited exceptions such as seed investments (up to 3% of the fund and 3% of Tier 1 capital) and de minimis investments held under one year.

Under the Community Reinvestment Act, CRA performance is rated Outstanding, Satisfactory, Needs to Improve, or Substantial Noncompliance based on lending, investment, and service tests. Low ratings can block merger or expansion applications.

Regulation Z's ability-to-repay (ATR) rule requires creditors to make a reasonable, good-faith determination of a borrower's ability to repay before making a mortgage, considering eight underwriting factors including income, assets, employment, credit history, and debt-to-income ratio.

RESPA requires a Loan Estimate within 3 business days of application, a Closing Disclosure 3 business days before consummation, an initial escrow statement, and annual escrow statements, and prohibits kickbacks and unearned fees between settlement service providers.

The CFPB Payday Lending Rule requires lenders of covered short-term loans (<=45 days) and longer-term balloon-payment loans to determine a borrower's ability to repay, and limits payment withdrawal re-attempts after two consecutive failures.
